title: Repositories and Dependency Resolution
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of repositories and dependency resolution using at least one correct term from the lesson.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Repositories and Dependency Resolution** as part of **Packages, Modules, Dependencies, and Build Tools**. Build reproducibility depends on the Gradle Wrapper, compatible plugin/toolchain versions, declared dependency scopes, and repeatable test/build commands. Use the subtopics—Dependency Repositories, Version Selection, Dependency Resolution Failures—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Real projects depend on reliable error handling, modular organization, reproducible builds, and safe language boundaries. This lesson helps turn isolated syntax into maintainable applications.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Build reproducibility depends on the Gradle Wrapper, compatible plugin/toolchain versions, declared dependency scopes, and repeatable test/build commands.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with dependency repositories. Then compare it with version selection. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: Dependency Repositories
items.text: Dependency Repositories is part of reproducible project configuration. Declare the dependency or plugin where it belongs, preserve a compatible version set, and use the Gradle Wrapper for repeatable builds.

items.title: Version Selection
items.text: Version Selection means checking the boundary between the language feature and its compiler, runtime, plugin, library, or target version. Pin the versions used by the project and verify documented support before depending on the behavior.

items.title: Dependency Resolution Failures
items.text: Dependency Resolution Failures helps make behavior observable and repeatable. Define the expected result, include a boundary or failure case, and preserve enough diagnostic information to locate the cause without leaking sensitive data.

content_blocks.expected_output: The build declares the Kotlin/JVM plugin, a repository, and Kotlin test dependency (configuration example).
content_blocks.run_instructions: Place the snippet in the matching Gradle Kotlin DSL or project file; verify plugin and library versions against the official project guide.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: The newest version of every plugin and library is always mutually compatible.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
